DESCRIPTION: Unique identifier of one public comment; the grain of the Data Grid
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The regulations.gov identifier for a single submission, and the grain of every row here. In the enriched CSV export the column is named commentId; it is mapped to id so both sources share one schema. Quote it when referring a comment back to the docket.

DESCRIPTION: Agency that owns the docket. CMS throughout both sample sets
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The agency the comment was submitted to. Constant across both supplied files, so it is useful as a provenance stamp rather than as a filter.

DESCRIPTION: Date the comment was posted publicly. Trimmed to a date from the source timestamp
LONG_DESCRIPTION: When the submission became public. The source CSV carries a full UTC timestamp; it is trimmed to a date because the time of day carries no analytical meaning here and a mixed-format column is harder to filter. It drives the comment-volume-over-time view.

DESCRIPTION: Submitter-supplied subject line. Often auto-generated and uninformative
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The subject line on the submission. In bulk dockets this is frequently an auto-generated string such as 'Comment on CMS-2022-0190-0002', so it is weak evidence of content. Prefer Comment_summary or COMMENT_CATEGORY when grouping.

DESCRIPTION: The full submitted text; the input to every stage of the pipeline
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The body of the submission and the only true source column in the pipeline. HTML entities from the export are decoded on load, so an apostrophe reads as an apostrophe rather than ’. Every enrichment column below is derived from this field.

DESCRIPTION: The rulemaking docket the comment belongs to
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Groups comments to the rule they respond to. Both supplied files are single-docket, so it is a provenance stamp here, but it is the join key if several dockets are ever loaded together.

DESCRIPTION: Number of files attached. DERIVED for the CSV source from attachmentLinks
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Present natively in the SIJ JSON. The enriched CSV export has no such column, so it is derived by counting the entries in attachmentLinks. A non-zero value means the comment text alone is not the whole submission, which matters when a summary looks unexpectedly thin.

DESCRIPTION: URLs of attached files, where the export supplied them
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The source URLs for any attachments. Empty throughout the supplied samples. Retained because it is the evidence behind attachmentCount and the only route to the attached content.

DESCRIPTION: Length of the comment in characters; computed by doSentimentAnalysis
LONG_DESCRIPTION: A structural metric written by doSentimentAnalysis. Useful for separating substantive submissions from one-line form letters before any semantic work is done. A value of zero marks an empty comment body, which the pipeline treats as Neutral rather than failing.

DESCRIPTION: Words in the comment; computed by doSentimentAnalysis
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The companion to character_count, produced by the same whitespace split the Python uses. It drives the word-count histogram in visualizeNLP, and the executive briefing counts comments over five words as substantive.

DESCRIPTION: Rule-based sentiment label from the Snowflake run: Positive, Negative or Neutral
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Written by categorizeText in Snowflake using a keyword-intersection rule, not a trained model. It is a proxy: it reads word presence, not meaning, so negation and sarcasm are invisible to it. Treat it as a triage signal for finding comments to read, never as a measured opinion.

DESCRIPTION: CMS policy domain assigned by keyword scoring; Uncategorized when nothing matched
LONG_DESCRIPTION: One of five CMS domains, assigned by counting how many of each domain's keywords appear in the comment. Uncategorized means no keyword matched at all and is a real finding rather than a gap: in the supplied CSV it is the second largest group, so a domain breakdown that hides it overstates how well the taxonomy fits.

DESCRIPTION: Extractive summary produced in JavaScript at run time; not stored in either file
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Produced by the summarizeText stage in the browser, by scoring sentences on term frequency and keeping the highest-scoring ones. It is EXTRACTIVE: every word appears in the original comment. This differs from the Snowflake implementation, which calls Cortex Summarize and generates abstractive text. The browser version exists so the workflow is demonstrable without a Snowflake session; it is not a reproduction of the Cortex output.
